title: Left derived squares under exact equivalences
statement: Let B,B′,H,H′ be abelian categories with independently chosen unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let E:B≌B′ and G:H≌H′ be additive equivalences. Let L:B→H and L′:B′→H′ be additive functors with an isomorphism L⋙G≅E⋙L′. For any left derived functors LF,LF′ specified by universal localization counits on their homotopy categories, there is a natural isomorphism LF⋙D(G)≅D(E)⋙LF′. No right-derived functor or boundedness assumption is required.

source.place: Tags 05RR and 0941; uniqueness of derived functors; exact-equivalence specialization

proof.text: An additive equivalence of abelian categories is exact and induces an equivalence of cochain-complex categories and derived categories, with the Q-factorization isomorphism. Use the existing exact-functor localization API.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the following coefficient paragraph

proof.text: Regard each left-derived counit as a universal right Kan-extension counit. Precomposing by the quotient from cochain complexes to the homotopy category preserves universality because precomposition with this quotient is fully faithful. The quotientCompQh isomorphism changes its source to Q. This is exactly the public derivedCochainCounit construction.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the following coefficient paragraph

proof.text: Precomposition and postcomposition by an equivalence induce equivalences of right-extension categories, so preserve their terminal objects. The ordinary square, mapped termwise, and the Q-factorization give two universal right extensions of isomorphic functors along isomorphic localization squares. RightKanExtensionUniqueOfIso gives the desired derived square. This argument does not identify any derived-category universes.
